title: Nalknad Aramane and the Haleri rulers
content: Kodagu District Administration states that Doddavira Rajendra built Nalknad Aramane near Yavakapadi between 1792 and 1794 after escaping Tipu Sultan's troops. The portal describes paintings and carvings in the palace, records Doddavira Rajendra's marriage there in 1796, and says the last Haleri ruler Chikka Veerarajendra later took shelter there. The site is now under the Archaeology Department, according to the district page.
source_org: Kodagu District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal page is undated and does not cite archival references; the dates and historical narrative are attributed to the district portal.
keywords: Kodagu Nalknad Aramane palace Doddavira Rajendra Haleri rulers Chikka Veerarajendra architecture history

title: Coffee hills and paddy lowlands west of Chikkamagaluru city
content: Chikkamagaluru's district tourism page describes the city as a divide between the district's Malnad and Maidan landscapes. It says the western hills have coffee plantations and low-lying paddy fields, illustrating how terrain and elevation correspond to different farming patterns within the district.
source_org: Chikkamagaluru District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The tourism page is undated and describes broad landscape patterns without crop-area or production statistics.

title: Government coffee research station near Segodu
content: The Chikkamagaluru district tourism portal notes that a Government of India coffee research station near Segodu works on developing new coffee varieties. The district page places this research institution in the wider coffee-growing landscape around Chikkamagaluru; it does not name specific varieties or report trial results.
source_org: Chikkamagaluru District Administration, Government of Karnataka

title: Sringeri Sharada Peetha and Vidyashankara Temple
content: The Chikkamagaluru district portal locates Sringeri on the Tunga River and describes the Sharada Peetha as a major pilgrimage centre. It attributes the Peetha's establishment to Adi Shankaracharya and describes Vidyashankara Temple as combining Chola, Dravida, Nagara and Chalukya architectural styles. The attribution is presented as the district portal's account.
source_org: Chikkamagaluru District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page is undated and does not cite a historical source for the foundation tradition; the architectural description is attributed to the district portal.

title: ZAHRS Shivamogga crop portfolio and research areas
content: The University of Agricultural and Horticultural Sciences lists the Zonal Agricultural and Horticultural Research Station at Shivamogga as established in 1976. Its stated crop portfolio includes paddy, maize, ragi, pulses, ginger, arecanut, turmeric, cocoa, banana, tobacco, mango and cashew. The listed research areas include arecanut, organic farming, cashew and watershed development.
source_org: University of Agricultural and Horticultural Sciences, Shivamogga
uncertainty: The station webpage does not date the crop list or report current acreage and production; station establishment year is reproduced as stated by the university.

title: CFMV-1 blast-tolerant finger millet at Shivamogga research station
content: The University of Agricultural and Horticultural Sciences lists CFMV-1 among the finger-millet varieties developed at its Shivamogga research station and describes it as biofortified and blast tolerant. No nutrient concentration or yield figure is included because the station page does not state a reporting or trial year for those measurements.

title: Iruvakki research station's hill-region crop mix
content: The University of Agricultural and Horticultural Sciences lists its Iruvakki research station in the Shivamogga region with crops including maize, paddy, arecanut, coconut, ginger, turmeric, coffee, pepper, mango, jackfruit and citrus. The station page identifies agroforestry as a research project, documenting a mixed-crop research focus relevant to the hill and plantation environment.
source_org: University of Agricultural and Horticultural Sciences, Shivamogga

title: Thirthahalli station crops and Malnad research topics
content: The University of Agricultural and Horticultural Sciences lists an Agricultural and Horticultural Research Station at Thirthahalli, established in 2008. Its crop list includes arecanut, black pepper, paddy, cocoa, coconut, rubber, coffee, nutmeg, ginger and cardamom. Research topics listed by the station include mango pickling varieties, jackfruit varieties for Malnad, and nutrient and disease management in arecanut.
source_org: University of Agricultural and Horticultural Sciences, Shivamogga
uncertainty: The page gives no reporting year, crop-area figures or research-result values; the station's stated establishment year is retained as a historical fact.

title: Keladi and Ikkeri in Shivamogga's Nayaka heritage
content: Shivamogga's Culture and Heritage page identifies Keladi as the first capital of the Keladi Nayakas and describes its Rameshvara, Veerabhadreshvara and Parvati temples and a museum holding copper inscriptions, palm leaves and coins from the Nayaka period. The same page describes Ikkeri as a later Nayaka capital and identifies the Aghoreshvara temple as its principal surviving monument, with a mixed architectural style.
source_org: Shivamogga District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The district heritage page is undated and does not cite the museum catalogue or architectural chronology.

title: Balligavi temples and Veerashaiva associations
content: Shivamogga's Culture and Heritage page describes Balligavi as a former capital of Banavasi rulers in the 12th century and associates the site with Veerashaiva figures including Allama Prabhu and Akka Mahadevi. It lists remains of temples, shrines, mastikals, viragals and nisidigals, including the Kedareshvara and Tripurantakeshvara temples.
source_org: Shivamogga District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal is undated and its historical attributions are not accompanied by references; no contested chronology beyond the page's description is asserted.

title: Koodali at the Tunga-Bhadra confluence
content: The Shivamogga district heritage page describes Koodali as the place where the Tunga and Bhadra rivers meet and flow onward together. It also identifies temples in the area, including Hoysala-period Rameshvara and Narasimha temples, and a monastery with shrines to Sharadamba and Shankaracharya. This record links the river geography to a distinct local religious heritage site.
source_org: Shivamogga District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal page is undated; the river confluence and temple descriptions are presented as the district's account, without separate hydrological or archaeological citations.
